item.title: Contact Recycling
item.description: Contact Recycling is a technique I’ve developed for Box2D and Box3D. First you might be wondering what is Box3D? More on that later. Contact Recycling can drastically improve rigid body simulation performance. It can make the process of computing contact points almost free. Further it can significantly improved stability. Contact Recycling is inspired as a combination of other techniques. I have not seen this specific technique used in other physics engines.

item.title: Predictive Joint Limits
item.description: Box2D has support for continuous collision. This solves the problem of fast moving objects passing through each other due to discrete time steps. The Box2D continuous collision algorithm uses a time of impact (TOI) collision algorithm along with time sub-stepping for the response. There are other artifacts due to discrete time steps. Joint limits can also suffer from fast movement. For example, consider a filing cabinet where the drawers use prismatic (slider) joints.
